KEY MESSAGE 1... 

High pressure overhead to our 
north holds on for one more afternoon today with mostly clear 
skies allowing for more seasonable highs in the upper 60s and 
mid 70s. High level clouds will begin to stream into the region 
from the south and east before thickening and lowering in areas 
south and east of the Capital Region towards sunset. 
North/northeast winds will be breezy through the evening and 
into tomorrow morning with gusts 20-30 mph across much of the 
region, as the surface pressure gradient tightens with the 
developing Nor'easter making its way up the coast to our south 
and east. Stronger wind gusts 45-50 mph are expected where a 
Wind Advisory is in effect from 2 pm today through Sunday 
morning for Litchfield County CT. The greatest gusts are 
expected to occur late tonight through Saturday night as the 
Nor'easter is at it's furthest west.

KEY MESSAGE 2... 

As of 3:00 PM EDT, the 996 hPa coastal low pressure system 
developing into a 980-990 hPa Nor'easter is currently positioned 
just off the coast in the Atlantic, north of the Carolinas and 
entering the Delmarva region. There is better consensus surrounding 
the track and timing among the deterministic global models, AI-GFS/AI-
ECMWF, and the ensembles continuing the slightly more south and 
western trend, however it still remains more impactful south of our 
CWA. Some of the latest CAMs, especially the NAM 3km shows a much 
more slow and more eastern track delaying the arrival of rain in the 
Albany area, but our forecast will favor the tighter cluster of the 
ensembles. Latest model runs show the associated sfc trough with the 
Nor'easter arriving a little later than previous allowing for an 
overcast, but mainly dry start to the day tomorrow with the cutoff 
low itself meandering to the south of Long Island through the day 
tomorrow. Some of the outer rain bands will begin to overspread 
areas south and east of Albany by tomorrow late afternoon/evening, 
but should still be intermittent and light initially. Saturday night 
into Sunday morning is really when the rain showers extend northward 
becoming a steadier light to moderate rain mainly I-90 south and 
east as the Nor'easter shifts westward tracking south of Long Island 
towards the NJ coast. The majority of guidance then has the system 
sitting and spinning off the NJ coast through much of Sunday before 
drifting slightly south and lifting back towards the northeast 
Sunday night into Monday. This is due to the lingering blocking high 
pressure system to our north and the nature of a cutoff low from 
steering flow. 

The areal extent and timing of the rainfall still has some 
uncertainty dependent on where the storm tracks however locations 
south and east of the Capital Region still have the best chance to 
receive the most rain with a sharp cutoff possible north of Albany. 
Expected rainfall totals from Saturday morning through Monday 
morning  have slightly increased with the greatest totals expected 
south and east of Albany, especially along the I-84 corridor. NBM 
probabilistic guidance has 70-80% chance for >1" for Southern 
Dutchess, Southern Ulster, and Litchfield counties, as well as higher 
terrain areas in the Catskills, Taconics, and the Berkshires. Areas 
in the Greater Capital District and Mohawk and Schoharie Valleys have 
a 40-60% chance for >1" and areas north and west of Albany have a 
20% or less chance for >1". There is a low chance of localized up to 
3" possible near I-84, however with dry antecedent soil conditions 
and rainfall being over a longer period, hydro concerns from 
rainfall will be minimal, outside of some ponding of water low lying 
and poor drainage areas and nuisance flooding in areas that 
typically flood. A River Flood Warning has been issued for the 
Hudson River near Poughkeepsie from tomorrow morning through 
tomorrow evening where a period of minor tidal flooding is expected 
to impact only the immediate coastline and docks along the river.

The main threat our region will see from this system is strong 
winds, especially tomorrow through Sunday night. Like with rainfall, 
the strongest gusts are expected to be areas south and east of 
Albany. Confidence has increased with NBM probabilistic guidance 
showing a 70-80% chance of >35 mph wind gusts across the Mid-Hudosn 
Valley, southern Catskills, Berkshires, and Litchfield County with a 
20-40% chance for the Capital Region and areas north. The greatest 
peak gusts (40-50 mph) will likely occur tomorrow afternoon where 
the Wind Advisory is in effect for Litchfield County with 
probabilistic guidance showing a 20% chance of wind gusts >45 mph 
which could knock down some foliated tree limbs, trees and produce 
some power outages. The H850 low-level jet increases from the N/NE 
at 40-60 KT along and south and east of the region however forecast 
soundings show a somewhat deep inversion in the 850-750 hPa layer 
which should help prevent gusts from exceeding 25-40 m
